automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.basis: Strict two-day public-source window relative to run timestamp
cutoff_window.date_policy: Included sources with visible publication or update dates inside the window. Excluded missing, ambiguous, future-dated, and boundary-only dates.

federation_policy.local_scope: Practice-level AI-assisted development implications, operating patterns, governance, verification, workflow, and adoption notes.
federation_policy.handling: Named ecosystem entities are recorded as upstream-owned. Findings include only the downstream practice implication or routing note.

findings.title: Copilot CLI can use GITHUB_TOKEN in GitHub Actions
findings.summary: GitHub says Copilot CLI can run inside GitHub Actions with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, using a copilot-requests: write workflow permission and organization billing instead of a long-lived PAT.
findings.why_it_matters: Agent automation guidance should prefer short-lived workflow identity, explicit permissions, and org-level spend controls over stored personal tokens for unattended coding-agent jobs.
findings.local_practice_implication: Source workflow pages can later describe token minimization and workflow permission scoping for coding-agent CI tasks without duplicating GitHub product documentation.
findings.routing_note: Route broad GitHub Copilot CLI product details to the upstream AI wiki.

findings.title: Copilot agent session records can stream to audit systems
findings.summary: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers with enterprise managed users can access Copilot agent session data across clients, including prompts, responses, and tool calls, by streaming to an event collector or SIEM or by using a REST API for the last 48 hours.
findings.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development governance is moving toward full agent-session observability, not just aggregate usage reporting. Audit patterns should account for prompts, responses, tool calls, retention windows, and SIEM routing.
findings.local_practice_implication: Governance pages can later define what teams should inspect in agent-session logs and how audit data supports post-incident review and evaluation loops.
findings.routing_note: Keep Copilot product coverage upstream; local wiki owns audit practice implications.

findings.title: Cost centers can cap included AI credit pool usage
findings.summary: GitHub added AI credit pools so enterprise cost centers can cap how much of the shared monthly included AI credit pool they consume before overage budgets apply.
findings.why_it_matters: Team adoption guidance should treat coding-agent usage as an accountable operating resource with chargeback boundaries, not only a per-seat enablement decision.
findings.local_practice_implication: Operating-model pages can later separate session-level guardrails, team budgets, and enterprise chargeback policy for AI-assisted development.
findings.routing_note: Route pricing and product-plan details upstream.

findings.title: Copilot CLI and SDK add per-session AI credit limits
findings.summary: GitHub added session limits for Copilot CLI and SDK so a session can cap AI-credit spend across model calls, subagents, and background work such as compaction; noninteractive runs can use a max-ai-credits limit.
findings.why_it_matters: Long-running coding-agent loops need explicit session budgets and graceful stop behavior, especially for unattended automation where no human is watching every turn.
findings.local_practice_implication: Agent workflow guidance can later include spend caps as part of run contracts for background repair, review, and research loops.
findings.routing_note: Keep feature mechanics upstream; capture local budget-control practice only.

findings.title: Enterprise managed-settings.json reaches GA
findings.summary: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers can maintain a managed-settings.json file in a .github-private repository to set enterprise AI standards for Copilot clients, including marketplaces, plugins, bypass-permission mode, and model settings.
findings.why_it_matters: Durable agent-instruction governance is becoming repository-backed and centrally refreshed, which affects how teams standardize allowed plugins, permission bypasses, and default model behavior.
findings.local_practice_implication: Prompt and instruction pages can later distinguish local project instructions from enterprise-managed AI client controls.
findings.routing_note: Route GitHub configuration reference details upstream.

findings.title: Enterprise admins can default Copilot to auto model selection
findings.summary: GitHub says enterprise administrators can set model to auto in managed-settings.json so new Copilot conversations start with automatic model selection, while users can still switch per conversation.
findings.why_it_matters: Model routing is becoming an enterprise-governed default. Practice guidance should treat model choice as a policy surface that balances reliability, cost, and task fit instead of a purely individual preference.
findings.local_practice_implication: Context architecture pages can later describe model routing as part of agent harness policy and evaluation design.
findings.routing_note: Keep model catalog and Copilot feature details upstream.

findings.title: Copilot browser tools in VS Code are generally available
findings.summary: GitHub made browser tools for Copilot in VS Code generally available. Agents can drive a real browser, navigate live web apps, and feed observations back into chat; the source notes permissions and enterprise controls.
findings.why_it_matters: Browser tool use turns live UI behavior into agent context. Practice guidance should require permission boundaries, network-domain controls, and verification expectations for browser-driven development or QA loops.
findings.local_practice_implication: Retrieval-and-tools and application-pattern pages can later cover when browser observation is evidence and when it still needs reproducible tests or logs.
findings.routing_note: Route VS Code and Copilot feature coverage upstream.

findings.title: Copilot vision is generally available
findings.summary: GitHub says Copilot vision is generally available, allowing images and PDFs in chat prompts across VS Code, github.com, and Copilot CLI. Business and Enterprise attachment retention is approximately 24 hours.
findings.why_it_matters: Multimodal context introduces retention and evidence-quality questions for AI-assisted development. Teams should decide which screenshots, PDFs, and diagrams are appropriate to send to coding agents.
findings.local_practice_implication: Context architecture and governance pages can later map multimodal inputs to privacy, retention, and citation rules.
findings.routing_note: Keep Copilot vision product scope upstream.

findings.title: Open-weight coding model option lands in Copilot
findings.summary: GitHub made Kimi K2.7 Code generally available in Copilot as an open-weight model option, initially rolling out to individual plans and off by default for Business and Enterprise until administrators enable the policy.
findings.why_it_matters: Model enablement policy now needs security, compliance, cost, and quality criteria, especially when models differ by openness, hosting, rollout scope, and administrative default.
findings.local_practice_implication: Verification-and-evals pages can later tie model enablement to evaluation gates and team-specific risk reviews instead of broad model descriptions.
findings.routing_note: Route model and hosting details upstream.

findings.title: Copilot plugin skill automates C++ compile command setup
findings.summary: GitHub added a Microsoft C++ Language Server plugin for Copilot CLI with a setup skill that generates or refreshes compile_commands.json for CMake and MSBuild projects and points custom build systems toward project-specific skills.
findings.why_it_matters: Code retrieval and editing quality depend on build-system-derived semantic context. Repeatable setup skills can turn fragile manual indexing steps into durable, source-specific context workflows.
findings.local_practice_implication: Retrieval-and-tools pages can later cover build-aware context generation as a prerequisite for reliable coding-agent edits.
findings.routing_note: Route plugin and language server product details upstream.

findings.title: Codex CLI stops writing full WebSocket payloads to trace logs
findings.summary: OpenAI's Codex changelog lists Codex CLI 0.142.5 with a bug fix preventing full Responses WebSocket request payloads from being written to trace logs.
findings.why_it_matters: Agent tracing is valuable for debugging but can become a sensitive-data exposure path. Local guidance should separate auditability from raw payload retention and define redaction expectations.
findings.local_practice_implication: Governance pages can later include trace-log hygiene for coding agents, especially when prompts or tool payloads may contain secrets, PII, or proprietary context.
findings.routing_note: Route Codex product release history upstream.

findings.title: Claude Code adds background-agent notifications and PR completion behavior
findings.summary: Claude Code 2.1.198 notes background agent notifications for sessions needing input or finishing, draft PR creation from completed worktree-based background code work, inherited extended-thinking configuration for subagents and compaction, and background subagents running by default.
findings.why_it_matters: Multi-agent coding workflows increasingly need explicit completion, input-needed, PR handoff, and inherited-reasoning-state practices so delegated work stays inspectable and recoverable.
findings.local_practice_implication: Agent workflow pages can later describe notification contracts and PR handoff gates for background coding sessions.
findings.routing_note: Route Claude Code product history upstream.
